LiberAI reports 36% success for Liber-0 on 60 new manipulation tasks

The model combines video, glove recordings and robot data, while difficult multi-step tasks remain substantially harder than pick-and-place.

The Robot Report ↗4 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 2

A company-reported evaluation

LiberAI described Liber-0 on November 4 in sponsored content in The Robot Report. Pretrained on more than 2.2 million hours of human experience, it achieved 36% overall success across 600 trials of 60 GPT-6-proposed tasks. These are company-reported results, not independent certification.

Connecting observation and action

Human video, LiberSense Glove motion recordings and an embodiment representation connect human experience to robot control. The model predicts future observations and actions together. Zero-shot here means no robot demonstrations collected specifically for the target tasks; robot data was still part of pretraining.

Complex manipulation remains difficult

Success was 63.5% for pick-and-place, 34% for other manipulation and 10.5% for the challenging or long-horizon group. The glove currently records hand poses and trajectories, not contact or force. Insertion, fastening and soft-material handling therefore remain important development areas. The evaluation does not establish general industrial readiness.
